message.content:
Here’s a classic set‑up for a hearty homemade lasagna (serves ~8–10 people). Feel free to tweak quantities or swap out items based on your taste.

| Category | Ingredient | Typical Amount |
|----------|------------|----------------|
| **Pasta** | Lasagna sheets (no‑boil or regular) | 9–12 sheets |
| **Meat Sauce** | Ground beef (or mix beef & pork) | 1 lb (≈450 g) |
| | Italian sausage (optional) | ½ lb (≈225 g), crumbled |
| | Onion, finely chopped | 1 small |
| | Garlic cloves, minced | 2–3 |
| | Crushed tomatoes / tomato sauce | 28 oz (800 ml) |
| | Tomato paste | 2 tbsp |
| | Red wine (optional) | ¼ cup |
| | Olive oil | 1–2 tsp |
| | Salt, pepper | To taste |
| | Dried oregano, basil, thyme | 1 tsp each |
| | Fresh parsley or basil (chopped) | 2 tbsp |
| | Sugar (if acidity needs balancing) | Pinch |
| **Ricotta Mixture** | Ricotta cheese | 16 oz (455 g) |
| | Egg (helps bind) | 1 large |
| | Grated Parmesan | ¾ cup (75 g) |
| | Nutmeg (freshly grated) | pinch |
| | Salt, pepper | To taste |
| **Mozzarella Layer** | Shredded mozzarella | 2 cups (180 g) |
| **Optional Extras** | Spinach (sautéed, drained) | 2 cups |
| | Mushrooms (sliced, sautéed) | 1 cup |
| | Bell peppers (diced) | ½ cup |
| | Carrot (grated) | ½ cup |

### Quick Prep Steps

1. **Cook Pasta:** Boil lasagna sheets until al dente; drain and lay flat on parchment paper so they don’t stick together.
2. **Make Meat Sauce:** Sauté onion/garlic → add ground meat + sausage → brown → stir in crushed tomatoes, pasta, wine, herbs, salt, pepper, sugar. Simmer 20–30 min.
3. **Prepare Ricotta Mix:** Combine ricotta, egg, parmesan, nutmeg, salt, pepper. Stir well.
4. **Layer:** In an oven‑proof dish, start with a thin layer of sauce, then sheets, ricotta mixture, optional veggies, more sauce, shredded mozzarella. Repeat layers ending with mozzarella on top.
5. **Bake:** Cover with foil (tent it over the pan if you want less browning) at 375°F (190°C) for 25 min, remove foil, bake another 10–15 min till bubbly and golden.
6. **Rest:** Let sit 10 minutes before slicing—this helps the layers set.

Enjoy! Adjust seasonings as you like, and feel free to experiment with different cheeses or adding béchamel for extra creaminess.
